cameron_miller2015.title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference

new_bank_questions.title: A cluster sandwich calculation
new_bank_questions.body: An intercept-only model has three independent clusters, each with two observations: $(1,2)$, $(3,4)$ and $(5,6)$. Compute the fitted mean, the bread $A$, the sum of squared cluster residual totals $B$, and the uncorrected sandwich variance $A^{-1}BA^{-1}$. Why should the usual large-cluster normal approximation be treated cautiously?
new_bank_questions.answer: The fitted mean is $3.5$. Cluster residual totals are $-4,0,4$, so $A=6$ and $B=16+0+16=32$. The variance is $32/36\approx0.8889$. With only three independent clusters the asymptotic normal approximation for inference can be poor.

shared_changes.description: The Sandwich estimator source excerpt states that the sandwich literally collapses to inverse information when working variance is true and that theory requires both cluster number and size grow. Qualify the first as equality of population/asymptotic formulas, and correct the second: many independent clusters suffice under bounded-cluster regularity. Opened Huber 1967 §4 corollary p. 231 and Cameron–Miller 2015 §II.C pp. 7–8. Retain all GEE/mean/working-covariance statements; inspect dependent marginal/GEE pages.
